Ensure TCP/HTTP upgrade support is enabled where needed. - If using TLS, terminate TLS at the Ingress (Ingress TLS) and proxy the WebSocket plain or wss to the backend, depending on your setup. - Ensure connection upgrade is allowed: the Ingress controller must pass WebSocket upgrade headers (Connection: Upgrade and Upgrade: websocket) and not terminate the protocol. - Configure timeouts and keep-alives as needed (e.g., upstream timeouts) to prevent idle disconnects. - Optional: use a separate Ingress rule per host/path, and set annotations on the Ingress to enable WebSocket support and proxy settings as required by your controller. Example high-level steps: 1) Deploy app - apiVersion: apps/v1 kind: Deployment metadata: { ... } spec: replicas: 2, template: containers: - name: ws-server image: your/wss:tag ports: [{ containerPort: 8080 }] 2) Service - apiVersion: v1 kind: Service metadata: { ... } spec: selector: { app: ws-server }, ports: [{ port: 80, targetPort: 8080 }] 3) Ingress (example for NGINX Ingress) - apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1 kind: Ingress metadata: { annotations: { "kubernetes.io/ingress.class": "nginx", "nginx.ingress.kateway.websocket": "true" } } spec: rules: - host: your.example.com http: paths: - path: / pathType: Prefix backend: service: name: ws-service port: number: 80 tls: - hosts: [your.example.com] secretName: tls-secret Notes: - WebSocket uses a persistent TCP connection upgraded from HTTP; nothing in HTTP polling is needed. - If you terminate TLS at the Ingress, your backend can speak plain WebSocket (ws) or you can pass through (wss) depending on your config. - Some Ingress controllers require specific annotations or config to enable proxy_http_version 1.1 and to propagate Upgrade/Connection headers; adjust per controller documentation.
